newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities ended mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities ended mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended mixed in moderate trade in retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.
"Both treasury bill yields and bond prices ended mixed across the board. The interbank rate rose slightly but it did not attract a lot of players," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 2.03/1.98 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.93/1.90 percent and one-year at a yield of 2.25/2.20 percent against 2.33/2.28 percent.
Among bonds, July 1998 ended at S$98.27/98.32 from Monday's close of S$98.20/98.25, September 2001 at S$97.00/97.05 versus S$97.15/97.20 and June 2003 at S$94.85/94.90 against S$95.10/95.15.
The overnight interbank offered rate rose to 3-1/2 3-3/8 percent from Monday's 3-1/4 3-1/8 percent.
